The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings; however, to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make a presentation shall be limited to three (3) minutes. MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA
  April 24, 2012

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was called to order
this day at 6:30 PM in the Council Chambers of City Hall by Mayor Bird.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEM(S)

No one came forward to speak.

ANY ITEM LISTED ON THE CLOSED SESSION TO THE OPEN SESSION AGENDA

MAYOR'S REPORT - MATTERS OF COMMUNITY INTEREST

Marvin Jackmon, SCE, resp for 4 cities on the Peninsula. PSE - if wires are down, please dial 911.
PowerPoint update of December 2011. February 29 V.P.s were present with city staff. Containment
Plan;- installing fault indicators in 12 areas on the Peninsula; most of them complete; some are
scheduled pending permits and notifications. 10 switches were planned. (see .pdf CPS) Switch
Over from overhead structures to be switched to Boxite Circuit. additional $1million, Proposed
Master Plan; a structured survey area established in this structured program which will take about
18 months for each of four phases'; $25 million per phase. Looked at various aspects to determine
needs for each area; $4 million on Peninsula this year, First area of attack is the PV Peninsula.
Funding through CPUC; they are still waiting for rate case decision; the amount of funds will be
determined to fund infrastructure work; decision expected later this year. Improvements update
included 2.5 miles of underground cable replacement on Bauxite circuit in the City; replaced bad
cable on PVDW and Via Montemar at a cost of $50,000; replaced bad cable on Margate and
Addition @ $50K; added two additional projects RH and RPV at a cost of $1 million to impove
reliability on the Peninsula. In December, questions were asked 1) LaCanada and invested
proportionately; 2) $100 million but can't spend more money than they get from CPUC; 3) Rate
case are not provided by City; they invest over entire territory they cover, not by City. 4) Electric
vehicles; 5) Research and going forward regarding undergrounding with Rule20 funds (no cost)
will determine if any parts fo the City would qualify, such as Lunada Bay; must be arterial street to
meet criteria and it might qualify and it would improvement reliability.

Councilmember Humphrey asked Mr. Jackmon was excited about the possibility of moving
forward with undergrounding projects and would appreciate reviewing with staff to resurrect some
of the projects that were previously determined to be cost effective. She asked about switchover
plans to the Bauxite site, esxcept for Via Borica, noting there were no outages in November thru
February no outages for Bauxite site; what is the timing; He confirmed they are scheduled to be
complete by May. Containment Plan switchover

Councilmember Perkins asked Mr. Jackmon to confirm Coveview will be switched to teh Bauxite
site. She asked how the rate case baseline would be. Mr. Jackmon responded that the utilities
rarely get what they ask for; hard to determine what final funding will be. Councilmember Perkins
asked if its set only at current rates will there be enough to go ahead with these projects; Jackmon
said they will get more than what they anticipate, and if that's the case these projects will go
forwarded.

Councilmember Rea asked if undewrground is prone to less outages; Jackmon said yes, generally,
less weather issues; more reliable than overhead. He asked about list of power outages provided;
what causes an underground cable to fail. Mr. Jackmon CIC cable installed without conduit
CITY COUNCIL
April 24, 2012

  2
 andthey failed and is deteriorating. He said it is not as part of Rule20; theya re not using 1970's
technology; there will be new cable underground.

MPT goodhart asked when they would hear status on the rate case approval $100 million+ on teh
Peninsula planned; he said it's larger than what was presented in December. He asked about the
band-aid or planned scope of work. He said they are using PVP as a template for other similar
communities. MPT Goodhart asked what is the back up plan if htey don't get the funding they
request. Mr. Jackmon said 9-12 years (3-4 years per rate case). He said there will be less outages;
the rate case is a big animal but they will get some funds they will look to areas where the help is
needed. La Canada and Santa Monica noted with similar problems; have the investment been the
sme in those aeras? Yes. They have had more tree issues and reliaibility issues; similar probls in
Santa Monica and Beverly Hills. Goodhart confirmed that anyone who wishes to weigh in on a
rate case may; rates for residents would go up. He confirmed with Mr. Jackmon that they expect to
complete last project in June or July; he would plan to return in late July or August.

9.  Appeal of Planning Commission Certification of EIR State Clearinghouse No.

Vickie Kroneberger confirmed public notice was given.

Director Rigg said he would provide highlights and history of findings. EIR for demolotion of
existing residence at 504 Paseo Del Mar. REviewed in June 2009, concerns were raised about
theimpacts of the project and historical of the house. Denied by teh Planning Commission. Staff
CITY COUNCIL
April 24, 2012

  6
 determined because existing residence required environmental review. He said we do not have a
historical ordinance; a draft EIR October 2010; comments were received and addressed in final
EIR, for public review in December. He said the EIR considered 4 alternatives to the project; each
of the alternatives were found to be unfeasible in teh final EIR (list reasons). All comments
received are in the final EIR. the NC and grading application were presented on December 20,
2011 to PC; voted 3-1 to certify the EIR, etc., but NC and grading were continued; on March 20,
2012, PC voted unanimouslys to approve the NC with conditions. Appeal filed on the EIR by Los
Angeles Conservancy; the City Council review was delayed while PC reviewed the NC. Appeal
states EIR fails....(list failures); the appeal does not appeal or challenge NC. He reviewed
alternatives available to the Council for consideration.

City Attorney Hogin said EIR are not seen frequently in a residential community; generally are
exempt, but not absolute. In this sitaution, the fact the house was built by Wright was unique and
worth a closer look. If there is evidence, the City is required to do full EIR; it had to be done. He
said the point of hte EIR is lay out the potential impacts and range of alternatives CC may consider.
The appeal complains about the reasonableness of the range of alternatives and questions that the
alternatives are unfeasible.

Councilmember Perkins said applicant prerogative to determine the project. Hogin said a
reasonable objective to have a usable backyard and usable house for owner. PC didn't rely on teh
ojbectives because of the age and status of structure.

Rea confirmed EIR was made by staff; this is first time before CC. Hogin confirmed; case law
would support, but the question is if it meets CQA.

MPT Goodhart asked if L.A. Conservancy questions have been responded to since the appeal was
provided. Hogin spoke about the draft and comments; final EIR questions that the responses were
not adequate in teh final EIR; the PC was satisfied that they were. Rigg said a professional
consultant prepared the EIR and responses; but PC ultimately made the decision that it was
acceptable.

MPT Goodhart said we do not have a historical structure ordinance; in CQA requirements, process
with 4 criteria established, but he did see if homeowner has the freedom to . Hogin said they are
lookinat at whether or not EIR prepared studied reasonable range and any/all feasible mitigation
measures to prevent any significant impact to cultural resource.

Adrian Scott Fein, Director of , L.A. Conservancy, said the Moore House is an architecturally
significant home of master Lloyd Wright, son of FLW, reason is based on state law and CQA
requirements with flawed EIR process to avoid significant impacts. Focus must be on EIR process;
personal preferences are not relevant and should override the process. He said EIR does not meet
evluation range of reasonable laternatives to void significanet effects of the prject. He sid the EIR
singel sincere preservation alternative (fails) logical and reasonable to analyze and not included n
EIR. He said a preservation alternative would meet standards. He said the final EIR does not
demonstrate good faith effort to preservation alternative. They met with owner; alternative B, the
EIR structurally or technically infeasible is not .... overriding considerations is generic and doesn't

CITY COUNCIL
April 24, 2012

  7
 provide substantial evidence and favors the applicant. Only alternative is to deny EIR.\\

Mark Paullin, applicant, 2101 Paseo Del Mar, owner 504, dream to be residents in Malaga Cove
and avaialability came on Paseo del Mar and they found there were no restrictions on demolition
and purchased. Presented a home to Planning Commission; it was found too high per neighborhood
opposition, complained to conservancy. They've since lowered the home and have support of
neighbors. He said it unusual to be required EIR. He said they are asking for a secure backyard; an
objective, they do not want a backyard that is too small. There is a view only from living room; it
did not satisfy their objectives. He said it extremely expensive to live in that house; they would
like a home that fits taht neighborhood. It's been a three year process and asked Council to uphold
PC decision.

SPEAKERS:

Terry Takeda, Hermosa Beach, historic structures define what people think about a City; sense of
what is our cities locally. sense of what identifies a City; L.A. County lacks that PVE does not have
historical strucutres in the MC evaluation; something the City may want to consider.

Steven Russo, Long Beach, said the City should be proud of having Lloyd Wright house; consider
this resource. Consider ordinance for historic purposes.

David Kobabe, 1708 Chelsea Road, supported Paullin for approval; this house does not fit
neighborhood or community; it is an eyesore. There are other homes that have historical
significance. This house is on remote and quiet street. Concerned about added traffic if required to

Regina O'Brian, Chair of Monarch (?), advocate and instrumental in saving L.A. icons, such as

 and developers.

Don Tuffle, 1412 Lower Paseo La Cresta, supported Paulins; new design great addition to

Phillip Dance, front bench balcony only 18 inches very dangerous to small children; unsafe.

Ann O'Brian, Hollywood Riviera, love historic prperties; Moore house represents advances that

Allan Hesse, architectural historian, Lloyd Wright is a major architect - progress, optimism,

Sal Gonzales, 453 Via Media, Art Jury process in 2002; part of appeal of LMC is the architecture

community; the house has become a blemish. No takers is puzzling.New home would beautify our

Sunny McBride, daring and exciting, but a miserable home. The interior and structure; unfortunate

CITY COUNCIL
April 24, 2012

  9
 Norman Eagle, 528 Via Media, poor opinion about the design from many. Most welcome a brand
new house; at first was not in support, but now on board and support applicant right to demolish the
house. He questioned benefit to preservation; no public access and has limited viewing from the

Julie Pond, 2631 Via Rivera, support applicant; the house is not livable and unfavorable to families;

Sherry Saperstein, Los Angeles, post war creative and culture celebrated throughout Southland.

Logan Madison, Long Beach, support the Conservancy; it is valuable architectural resource.
Polarization

Chris Vancura, 509 PDM, impacts to him and wondered how it was approved in the first place;

Dana Hutch, architectural historian/author, lack of compromise a shame; potential loss of historical

Charles Peterson, Via Valmonte, support Paullin's project. EIR thoroughly addressed reuse

John Tolchian, 2329 Chelsea, community overwhelmingly supports applicant; it is an eyesore in

April 24, 2012

 Mr. Fein, LA Conservancy standpoint appreciate all comments. Mid century architecture is
discussion spoken across the country; heritage; it is historic. They are doing this because of hte

(Chang also questioned) issues unsupported; it is a matter of CEQA law; public agency

councilmember Rea said the Paullin letter obstructed efforts to give away the house. Mr. Fein said

Mr. McMurray, on behalf of Mr. Paullin, can't significantly modify or take down his house. L.A.
Conservancy does not provide alternatives. All 70 Lloyd Wright houses in California to be
preserved in perpetuity? In this case, he didn't think this is the right decision.

MPT Goodhart closed the public hearing.

City Attorney Hogin no harm no foul fluidity of EIR and PC recommendaiton isn't dependent on
any specific objective that standsin the way founding a preservation alternative. He siad other
alternatives keep outside of home, or facade, and then moving it entirely. EIR found issues with

Considerations testimony undersold what PC found; it is a matter of community concern about

 City has NC ordinance, unique, fairly descriptive of its purpose. Fits in with neighborhood;
